Obtuse

ub-TOOS -- two syllables, stress on the second syllable, TOOS. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Obtuse is annoyingly stupid or insensitive.

Marcus was being deliberately obtuse about whose turn it was to do the dishes, though the chore chart hung right beside him.

Worked Example

Everyone at the meeting has said, three different ways, that the deadline cannot be met. The new supervisor nods along, then asks brightly, 'So we're all set for Friday, then?'

The supervisor is being obtuse: annoyingly slow to grasp what is obvious to everyone else in the room. Obtuse can describe genuine dullness or -- very often -- a convenient, deliberate refusal to understand.

How Obtuse Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

dense

dense: slow to understand

dim-witted

dim-witted: lacking quickness of mind

Antonyms

sharp

sharp: quick to notice and understand

quick-witted

quick-witted: fast to grasp and respond

How Strong Is It? — dense → obtuse → dim-witted

dense vs. obtuse

dense vs. obtuse: Dense is the everyday word for slow understanding, while obtuse adds the sting of annoyance -- an obtuse listener is missing something so obvious that everyone else is losing patience.

dim-witted vs. obtuse

dim-witted vs. obtuse: Dim-witted is the strongest and least kind: it declares the mind itself slow, while obtuse often accuses someone of CHOOSING not to understand -- being deliberately obtuse is a strategy, not a limitation.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ob-

prefix — ob-: against (Latin)

root — tuse

root — tuse: beaten, blunted (Latin tundere, tusus 'to beat')

Put it together

Put it together: Obtuse comes from Latin obtusus, 'beaten against' -- a blade hammered until its edge is blunt. An obtuse mind is a blunted one: no edge, no point, unable (or unwilling) to cut through to what is obvious.

Use the root in a new word: contusion

Use the root in a new word: contusion: The doctor said the swelling was only a contusion -- a deep bruise from the fall.

Root Check

Word Choice

Obtuse is a criticism of understanding, and it often implies choice: 'deliberately obtuse' is one of the word's favorite pairings. Use it for people and their refusals to see the obvious -- its sting lands harder than dense, because it accuses the listener of failing at something everyone else found easy.
